niche.title: Niche
niche.description: What the businesses do — `frizerski salon`, `teretana`, `restoran`, `zubar`. For the OpenStreetMap source you can also pass a raw OSM tag such as `shop=hairdresser`.

city.title: City
city.description: Where to look. For OpenStreetMap use the local name — `Beograd`, not `Belgrade` — because it matches the administrative boundary by name.

queries.title: Explicit search phrases
queries.description: Overrides `niche` + `city` for the Google Maps source. Use it when you want full control over the phrasing.

source.title: Source
source.description: **Google Maps** has by far the best coverage but needs a browser and gets CAPTCHA'd without residential proxies. **OpenStreetMap** covers less but is a free public API that never blocks you — the dependable option for unattended local runs. **Both** merges and de-duplicates them.
enumTitles: Google Maps — best coverage, gets blocked

maxResultsPerQuery.title: Max results per query
maxResultsPerQuery.description: Google Maps itself stops at roughly 100-120 places per search, so going much higher only lengthens the run.

languageCode.title: Google language
languageCode.description: The `hl` parameter. Affects result ranking and the labels the panel renders.

enrichFromWebsite.title: Scrape each website for contacts
enrichFromWebsite.description: Where the e-mails actually come from — Google Maps shows a website, almost never an address. Requests go to the business's own server, so no Google limit applies.

maxWebsitePagesPerLead.title: Max website pages per lead
maxWebsitePagesPerLead.description: Landing page included. If it holds no address, the usual contact pages are tried next.

onlyWithEmail.title: Only save leads that have an e-mail

emailDomainBlocklist.title: Ignored e-mail domains
emailDomainBlocklist.description: Added to the built-in list of tracker and placeholder domains. An entry blocks its subdomains too.

verifyEmailDomains.title: Verify addresses (MX + classification)
verifyEmailDomains.description: One cached DNS query per domain. Adds `emailDetails` to every lead: whether the domain accepts mail at all, and whether the address is a role account (`info@`), a free-mail box (`gmail.com`) or a disposable one.
verifyEmailDomains.sectionDescription: Sending to dead addresses is what wrecks a sending domain's reputation, and that damage is slow to undo. This check costs one DNS lookup per domain.

dropUndeliverable.title: Drop addresses whose domain has no mail server
dropUndeliverable.description: Removes them from `emails` instead of only labelling them. Disposable providers are always dropped when verification is on.

dropRoleAccounts.title: Drop role accounts
dropRoleAccounts.description: Removes `info@`, `office@`, `prodaja@` and similar. Off by default: for small businesses that is very often the only published address, so dropping them guts the list.

placeSelectors.title: Place panel selectors
placeSelectors.description: Escape hatch for when Google changes the Maps layout. Override only the keys that broke — `name`, `website`, `phone`, `address`, `category`, `rating`, `feed`, `placeLink`. Example: `{ "website": "a[data-item-id='authority']" }`.
placeSelectors.sectionDescription: The Maps DOM is generated and unversioned. These defaults target data-item-id and ARIA attributes, which survive restyling better than class names — but when a run suddenly returns names and nothing else, this is the place to fix it.

placeDelayMs.title: Delay between places (ms)
placeDelayMs.description: Pacing between opening one place panel and the next.

proxyConfiguration.title: Proxy
proxyConfiguration.description: Residential proxies are close to mandatory for the Google Maps source at any real volume. The OpenStreetMap source does not need one.
